title: Document Outline Template
body:
# Document Outline Template

This template defines the structural scaffold for a document outline conforming to `outline.json` schema. The outline is produced after the brief is approved and before any section drafting begins. Every section_drafter receives an outline entry as their primary input — the quality of the outline directly determines the quality of the draft.

---

## Outline JSON Structure

```json
{
  "title": "[Full document title — specific, not generic]",
  "document_type": "[article|memo|spec|lore|flavor-text|report]",
  "domain": "[general|technical|internal|dnd|card-game]",
  "brief_id": "[Reference ID of the approved brief this outline serves]",
  "target_word_count": 0,
  "style_pack": "[Name of the active style pack]",
  "sections": []
}
```

---

## Section Entry Structure

Each entry in the `sections` array must include all of the following fields:

```json
{
  "id": "S[N]",
  "title": "[Specific, reader-oriented section title]",
  "purpose": "[One sentence: what job this section does for the reader]",
  "required_content": [
    "[Specific claim or point that must appear in this section]",
    "[Another required element — not vague, not generic]"
  ],
  "scope_notes": "[What this section explicitly does NOT cover — prevents overlap]",
  "estimated_word_count": 0,
  "subsections": []
}
```

### Field Guidance

**id:** Sequential identifiers (S1, S2, S3...). Subsection IDs use dot notation: S1.1, S1.2. The section-drafter uses this ID to register its output in the merge-normalizer handoff.

**title:** The title must be specific enough that a section-drafter knows what to write without reading the scope notes. "Background" is not a good title. "Why Traditional Recommendation Approaches Break at Scale" is a good title.

**purpose:** One sentence describing what the reader gains from this section. Forces the outline-architect to justify every section's existence. If you cannot state the reader-facing purpose, the section may not be necessary.

**required_content:** A list of specific claims, facts, examples, or arguments that must appear. This is the outline-architect's binding instruction to the section-drafter. Vague entries like "discuss the topic" are not valid. Each entry should be specific enough that the section-drafter cannot miss it.

**scope_notes:** Declares what this section does not cover, especially where adjacent sections might overlap. Prevents both duplication and gaps in multi-section documents.

**estimated_word_count:** The section-drafter uses this as a ceiling. Sum of all section word counts must equal or approximate the brief's target_word_count. Allocate proportionally to section importance, not section position.

**subsections:** Array of nested section entries using the same structure. Use subsections when a section has two or more logically distinct sub-topics that each require their own scope declaration. Do not nest more than two levels deep.

---

## Outline Quality Checklist

Before delivering the outline, verify: (1) every section has a testable purpose, (2) no two sections have overlapping scope, (3) section sequence follows the reader's comprehension needs (not the writer's convenience), (4) word count allocations sum to the brief target, (5) each required_content entry is specific.
